step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture represents Lockheed Martin's voice-activated Program Management status solution using AWS. Mobile users access the app via Alexa for Business, triggering the PM Skill Lambda. This Lambda queries an RDS (Aurora MySQL) database for program statuses and consults DynamoDB to format abbreviations/acronyms for proper voice synthesis. On the data ingestion side, two separate S3 buckets receive Excel spreadsheets containing program data and abbreviation lists. Each bucket triggers an ingestion Lambda function to parse and store the data into RDS and DynamoDB respectively.

nodes.name: Abbreviations S3 Bucket

nodes.name: Abbreviations Ingestion Lambda

edges.notes: Mobile app sends user voice requests to Alexa for Business.
Alexa for Business triggers the PM Skill Lambda function.
PM Skill Lambda queries program status data from RDS.
RDS returns program status records to PM Skill Lambda.
PM Skill Lambda checks DynamoDB for acronym pronunciation formatting.
S3 upload event triggers the Data Ingestion Lambda.
Data Ingestion Lambda parses Excel data into columnar format and inserts it into RDS.
S3 upload event triggers the Abbreviations Ingestion Lambda.
Abbreviations Ingestion Lambda creates key-value pairs and writes them to DynamoDB.
